title: Violin teaching survey
intro: We built a computer program that watches and listens to someone playing the violin and keeps track of {n} different things. Each card describes one of them in everyday words. For each one, tell us two things: do violin teachers care about it, and could a student use the number? There are no right or wrong answers.

questions.h1: Do violin teachers pay attention to {x} in lessons?
questions.h2: If a practice app gave a student a number for {x}, could the student act on it?
questions.h2_gloss: We mean the number itself. Could a student practise differently because of it?

rows.name: Where the bow touches the string, compared with the player's usual spot

phrases.source: Fischer, The Violin Lesson (2013)
Flesch, The Art of Violin Playing, Book 1

phrases.text: the bow drifting from the contact point
phrases.source: Starr, The Suzuki Violinist
Lin Yaoji, teaching maxim, in Yang Baozhi, Essentials of Lin Yaoji's Violin Teaching Method (2004)

rows.definition: Whether the bow is touching the string closer to the bridge or closer to the fingerboard than this player usually does.
rows.unit: a share of the string's length
rows.range: 0 = the player's usual spot; below 0 = closer to the bridge than usual; above 0 = closer to the fingerboard than usual
rows.prose: This records where the bow touches the string and compares it with the spot this player normally uses. The number is zero at the usual spot, below zero when the bow is nearer the bridge than usual, and above zero when it is nearer the fingerboard. Teachers call this spot the "sounding point" or "contact point".
rows.short: where the bow touches the string

rows.name: Which part of the bow is on the string

phrases.text: at the frog / in the middle / at the tip

phrases.source: ViolinITS etude classification spreadsheet, columns "Equal length, 2 bow length, 3-4 bow length"
Fischer, The Violin Lesson (2013)

rows.definition: Whether the player is using the bow near the frog (the hand end), the middle, or the tip.
rows.unit: a share of the bow's length
rows.range: 0 = at the frog; 0.5 = the middle of the bow; 1 = at the tip
rows.prose: This records which part of the bow is on the string: near the hand end (the frog), the middle, or the tip. The number is 0 at the frog, 0.5 in the middle and 1 at the tip. Teachers talk about playing "at the frog" or "at the tip".
rows.short: which part of the bow is on the string

rows.name: Is the bow on the string or lifted off?

phrases.text: bow on the string / off the string

phrases.source: ViolinITS etude classification spreadsheet

rows.definition: How far the bow hair is from the string: zero when the bow is on the string, more when it is lifted off.
rows.unit: a share of the string's length
rows.range: 0 = on the string; bigger = lifted further off
rows.prose: This records whether the bow is touching the string or lifted off it. The number is zero when the bow is on the string and grows as the bow lifts higher. Teachers speak of playing "on the string" or "off the string".
rows.short: whether the bow is on the string or lifted off

rows.name: Is the bow straight or crooked?

phrases.source: Hamann & Gillespie, Strategies for Teaching Strings (4th ed., 2018)
Provenzale et al. (2024), Sensors

rows.definition: How far the bow is from being at a right angle to the strings, in other words how crooked the bow stroke is.
rows.unit: degrees
rows.range: 0 = perfectly straight; bigger = more crooked, in either direction
rows.prose: This records whether the bow is straight or crooked, in other words whether it crosses the strings at a right angle. The number is zero for a perfectly straight bow and grows as the bow gets more crooked. Teachers say "keep the bow straight" or "your bow is crooked".
rows.short: how straight the bow is

rows.name: Which string the bow is leaning toward

phrases.source: Galamian, Principles of Violin Playing and Teaching (1962); Rolland, The Teaching of Action in String Playing (1974)
Provenzale et al. (2024), Sensors

rows.definition: The tilt of the bow around the strings, which shows which string it is playing on or moving toward.
rows.unit: degrees
rows.range: smaller = toward the G string (the lowest); larger = toward the E string (the highest)
rows.prose: This records which string the bow is leaning toward. Lower numbers mean the bow is leaning toward the G string, the lowest one; higher numbers mean toward the E string, the highest one. Teachers talk about "string crossing".
rows.short: which string the bow is leaning toward

rows.name: Bow speed (with direction)

phrases.source: Fischer, The Violin Lesson (2013); Flesch, The Art of Violin Playing, Book 1

phrases.text: It is impossible to scratch if the bow keeps moving
phrases.source: Fischer, The Violin Lesson (2013), chapter heading
Lin Yaoji, teaching maxim, in Yang Baozhi, Essentials of Lin Yaoji's Violin Teaching Method (2004)

rows.definition: How fast the bow is moving, and whether it is going down-bow or up-bow.
rows.unit: bow-lengths per second (1 = a full bow in one second)
rows.range: 0 = the bow is not moving; above 0 = down-bow; below 0 = up-bow
rows.prose: This records how fast the bow is moving, and whether it is a down-bow or an up-bow. The number is zero when the bow is still, above zero for a down-bow and below zero for an up-bow; the bigger the number, the faster the bow. Teachers call this "bow speed".
rows.short: bow speed

rows.name: Bow speed (without direction)

phrases.source: Fischer, The Violin Lesson (2013); Flesch, The Art of Violin Playing, Book 1
Fischer, The Violin Lesson (2013), chapter heading

rows.definition: How fast the bow is moving, whether it is a down-bow or an up-bow.
rows.unit: bow-lengths per second (1 = a full bow in one second)
rows.range: 0 = not moving; bigger = faster
rows.prose: This records how fast the bow is moving, without caring whether it is a down-bow or an up-bow. The number is zero when the bow is still, and the bigger the number, the faster the bow. Teachers call this "bow speed".
rows.short: bow speed regardless of direction

rows.name: How quickly the bow speeds up or slows down

phrases.text: speeding up or slowing down the bow within a stroke

phrases.source: ViolinITS etude classification spreadsheet

rows.definition: Whether the bow is speeding up, slowing down, or moving at a steady speed during a stroke.
rows.unit: change in bow speed per second
rows.range: 0 = steady speed; bigger = the speed is changing more quickly
rows.prose: This records whether the bow is speeding up, slowing down, or keeping a steady speed during a stroke. The number is zero for a steady speed, and the bigger the number, the faster the speed is changing. Teachers talk about "speeding up" or "slowing down" the bow within a stroke.
rows.short: how quickly the bow speeds up or slows down

rows.name: Down-bow or up-bow
rows.definition: Whether the bow is moving as a down-bow or an up-bow, passing smoothly through zero when it turns around.
rows.unit: a value between −1 and +1
rows.range: +1 = clearly down-bow; −1 = clearly up-bow; near 0 = stopped or changing direction
rows.prose: This records whether the bow is moving as a down-bow or an up-bow. The number is +1 for a clear down-bow, −1 for a clear up-bow, and near zero while the bow is stopped or turning around. Teachers say "down-bow" and "up-bow".
rows.short: whether the bow is going down or up

rows.name: How bent the bow-arm elbow is

phrases.text: elbow angle / elbow height of the bow arm

phrases.source: Rolland, The Teaching of Action in String Playing (1974); Galamian, Principles (1962)

phrases.text: changing notes without changing the arm shape
phrases.source: Lin Yaoji, in Yang Baozhi (2004); English rendering only in our reading notes

rows.definition: How much the right elbow is bent, estimated from a computer model of the player's body.
rows.unit: degrees (an estimate from a body model, not a medical measurement)
rows.range: 0 = arm straight; bigger = more bent
rows.prose: This records how much the elbow of the bow arm is bent. The number is zero for a straight arm, and the bigger the number, the more the elbow is bent. Teachers talk about the "elbow" being too high or too low, and about "whole-arm strokes".
rows.short: how bent the bow-arm elbow is

rows.name: Bow-hand wrist turn, direction 1 of 3

phrases.source: Rolland, The Teaching of Action in String Playing (1974)
ViolinITS schema leaf

rows.definition: One of three ways the bow-hand wrist can turn, as a computer body model measures it, compared with this player's usual wrist position. The three directions belong to the model; they are not the words a teacher would use, such as "bent" or "flexed".
rows.unit: degrees (an estimate from a body model, not a medical measurement)
rows.range: 0 = the player's usual wrist position; above or below 0 = turned one way or the other
rows.prose: Our system watches the wrist of the bow hand and records how it is turned. It splits that turn into three directions, a bit like bending the wrist up and down, tilting it from side to side, and twisting it, though we cannot say exactly which direction is which. This card is about direction 1 of the three. The number is zero when the wrist is in the player's usual position, and it goes up or down as the wrist turns away from that. Teachers do not have a word for this; the closest is a "bent wrist".
rows.short: how the bow-hand wrist is turned

rows.name: Bow-hand wrist turn, direction 2 of 3

phrases.source: Rolland, The Teaching of Action in String Playing (1974)
ViolinITS schema leaf

rows.definition: One of three ways the bow-hand wrist can turn, as a computer body model measures it, compared with this player's usual wrist position. The three directions belong to the model; they are not the words a teacher would use, such as "bent" or "flexed".
rows.unit: degrees (an estimate from a body model, not a medical measurement)
rows.range: 0 = the player's usual wrist position; above or below 0 = turned one way or the other
rows.prose: Our system watches the wrist of the bow hand and records how it is turned. It splits that turn into three directions, a bit like bending the wrist up and down, tilting it from side to side, and twisting it, though we cannot say exactly which direction is which. This card is about direction 2 of the three. The number is zero when the wrist is in the player's usual position, and it goes up or down as the wrist turns away from that. Teachers do not have a word for this; the closest is a "bent wrist".
rows.short: how the bow-hand wrist is turned

rows.name: Bow-hand wrist turn, direction 3 of 3

phrases.source: Rolland, The Teaching of Action in String Playing (1974)
ViolinITS schema leaf

rows.definition: One of three ways the bow-hand wrist can turn, as a computer body model measures it, compared with this player's usual wrist position. The three directions belong to the model; they are not the words a teacher would use, such as "bent" or "flexed".
rows.unit: degrees (an estimate from a body model, not a medical measurement)
rows.range: 0 = the player's usual wrist position; above or below 0 = turned one way or the other
rows.prose: Our system watches the wrist of the bow hand and records how it is turned. It splits that turn into three directions, a bit like bending the wrist up and down, tilting it from side to side, and twisting it, though we cannot say exactly which direction is which. This card is about direction 3 of the three. The number is zero when the wrist is in the player's usual position, and it goes up or down as the wrist turns away from that. Teachers do not have a word for this; the closest is a "bent wrist".
rows.short: how the bow-hand wrist is turned

rows.name: Bow-arm shoulder position, compared with the player's usual

phrases.source: Rolland, The Teaching of Action in String Playing (1974)
Havas, A New Approach to Violin Playing (1961)

phrases.text: let the violin become part of the body
phrases.source: Lin Yaoji, in Yang Baozhi, Essentials of Lin Yaoji's Violin Teaching Method (2004)

rows.definition: How much the right shoulder has moved away from this player's usual shoulder position, for example raised or hunched.
rows.unit: degrees (an estimate from a body model, not a medical measurement)
rows.range: 0 = the usual position; bigger = further from it
rows.prose: This records how far the bow-arm shoulder has moved away from the position this player normally holds it in, for example when the shoulder rises or hunches. The number is zero in the usual position, and the bigger the number, the further the shoulder has moved. Teachers warn about a "raised shoulder".
rows.short: the bow-arm shoulder position

rows.name: Head tilt

phrases.source: ViolinITS schema leaf

rows.definition: How far the head and neck are tilted away from upright, in any direction.
rows.unit: degrees (an estimate from a body model)
rows.range: 0 = upright; bigger = more tilted
rows.prose: This records how far the head is tilted away from upright, in any direction. The number is zero when the head is upright, and the bigger the number, the more it is tilted. Teachers talk about "head position".
rows.short: head tilt

rows.name: Posture: upright or slouched

phrases.source: Kreitman, Teaching from the Balance Point (1998); Flesch, The Art of Violin Playing, Book 1; Gruenberg (1919)
Rolland, The Teaching of Action in String Playing (1974)

rows.definition: How much the upper body is bent forward or sideways from upright.
rows.unit: degrees (an estimate from a body model)
rows.range: 0 = upright; bigger = more bent
rows.prose: This records how much the upper body is bent forward or sideways instead of standing upright. The number is zero when upright, and the bigger the number, the more the body is bent. Teachers call this "posture" or "slouching".
rows.short: posture

rows.name: How high the violin is held

phrases.source: Auer, Violin Playing as I Teach It (1921)

phrases.text: violin drifting over the right arm
phrases.source: Starr, The Suzuki Violinist
Rolland, The Teaching of Action in String Playing (1974)

phrases.text: let the violin become part of the body
phrases.source: Lin Yaoji, in Yang Baozhi, Essentials of Lin Yaoji's Violin Teaching Method (2004)

rows.definition: How high the violin sits compared with the player's hips: lower when the scroll droops, higher when the violin is held up.
rows.unit: a share of the string's length (so body size does not matter)
rows.range: bigger = the violin is held higher
rows.prose: This records how high the violin is held compared with the player's hips: lower when the scroll droops, higher when the violin is held up. The bigger the number, the higher the violin. Teachers warn about a "drooping scroll".
rows.short: how high the violin is held

rows.name: In tune, sharp, or flat

phrases.source: Galamian, Principles of Violin Playing and Teaching (1962)
Fischer, Basics (1997), section F heading
feedback wording in the experimental literature (Salzberg 1980)
Xiao Ke (2016); Ma Xishui (2002), article titles
Lin Yaoji, teaching maxim, in Yang Baozhi, Essentials of Lin Yaoji's Violin Teaching Method (2004)

rows.definition: How far the note played is from the note written in the music.
rows.unit: semitones (the distance between two neighbouring piano keys; 100 cents)
rows.range: 0 = in tune; above 0 = sharp; below 0 = flat; 0.5 = a quarter-tone off
rows.prose: This records whether each note is in tune and, if not, how far off it is. The number is zero when the note is in tune, above zero when it is sharp (too high) and below zero when it is flat (too low). Teachers call this "intonation".
rows.short: whether a note is in tune, sharp or flat

rows.name: Loudness

phrases.source: ViolinITS etude classification spreadsheet, "Tone" columns
Auer, Violin Playing as I Teach It (1921), chapter topic

rows.definition: How loud the sound is from moment to moment.
rows.unit: decibels
rows.range: higher = louder; very low = silence
rows.prose: This records how loud the playing is from moment to moment. The bigger the number, the louder the sound; very low numbers mean silence. Teachers talk about "dynamics" or "volume".
rows.short: loudness

rows.name: How strongly each note starts

phrases.source: Cavitt (2003), teacher correction targets (band rehearsals)
ViolinITS etude classification spreadsheet, "Bow strokes" columns
Fischer, Basics (1997), section C

phrases.text: attack / the start of the note

rows.definition: How clearly and strongly a new note begins: high for a crisp, accented start, low in the middle of a held note.
rows.unit: a score with no unit
rows.range: 0 = no note starting; bigger = a stronger start
rows.prose: This records how clearly and strongly each note starts. The number is high for a crisp, accented start and low in the middle of a long, held note. Teachers talk about the "attack" of a note.
rows.short: how strongly each note starts

rows.name: The note being played

phrases.source: Galamian, Principles of Violin Playing and Teaching (1962)
Hamann & Gillespie, Strategies for Teaching Strings (4th ed., 2018)
Lin Yaoji, teaching maxim, in Yang Baozhi, Essentials of Lin Yaoji's Violin Teaching Method (2004)
Xiao Ke (2016); Ma Xishui (2002), article titles

rows.definition: Which pitch the violin is sounding at each moment, tracked continuously, so vibrato, slides and tuning all show.
rows.unit: piano-key numbers, with fractions in between
rows.range: higher = a higher note
rows.prose: This records which note the violin is sounding at every moment, including the small wobbles of vibrato and the slides between notes. Higher numbers mean higher notes. Teachers talk about "the note you are playing".
rows.short: the note being played

rows.name: How clean and clear the tone is

phrases.text: It is impossible to scratch if the bow keeps moving
phrases.source: Fischer, The Violin Lesson (2013), chapter heading
Hamann & Gillespie, Strategies for Teaching Strings (4th ed., 2018)
Suzuki, as described in Starr, The Suzuki Violinist
Lin Yaoji, teaching maxim, in Yang Baozhi, Essentials of Lin Yaoji's Violin Teaching Method (2004)

rows.definition: How clearly a definite note can be heard in the sound: high for a clean, focused tone, low for scratchy, noisy or silent moments.
rows.unit: a score with no unit
rows.range: near 0 = no clear note (silence or noise); bigger = a clearer tone
rows.prose: This records how clean and clear the tone is. The number is high for a clear, focused sound and low when the sound is scratchy, noisy, or silent. Teachers talk about a "clean tone" or a "scratchy tone".
rows.short: how clean and clear the tone is

rows.name: Played on a different string than the music suggests

phrases.text: wrong string / play it on the A string

phrases.source: ViolinITS etude classification spreadsheet, metadata column

phrases.text: building stepwise fingers on one string (D)
phrases.source: ViolinITS etude classification spreadsheet, goal text

rows.definition: How likely it is that the player used a different string from the one the written music points to.
rows.unit: a score from 0 to 1
rows.range: 0 = the same string the music suggests; 1 = clearly a different string; blank when the music does not say
rows.prose: This records whether a note was played on a different string from the one the sheet music suggests. The number is zero when it is the same string and 1 when it is clearly a different string; it is left blank when the music does not suggest a string. Teachers say "wrong string" or "play it on the A string".
rows.short: whether the player used a different string than the music suggests

rows.name: Left-hand position, compared with what the music suggests

phrases.source: Fischer, The Violin Lesson (2013), lesson topic; Fischer, Basics (1997), section E "Shifting"
ViolinITS etude classification spreadsheet, "Hand Frame" columns
Gerle, The Art of Practising the Violin (1983)
Ding Zhinuo, Intensive Training Materials for Violin Fundamentals (Shanghai Music Publishing House)

rows.definition: Whether the left hand was higher or lower on the fingerboard than the position the written music points to.
rows.unit: semitones along the string
rows.range: 0 = the expected position; above 0 = higher up the fingerboard; below 0 = lower
rows.prose: This records whether the left hand was higher or lower on the fingerboard than the sheet music suggests. The number is zero in the expected position, above zero when the hand is higher up and below zero when it is lower. Teachers talk about "positions" and "shifting".
rows.short: the left-hand position

rows.name: The player's usual bow-contact spot

phrases.source: Fischer, The Violin Lesson (2013)
Flesch, The Art of Violin Playing, Book 1

phrases.text: the bow drifting from the contact point
phrases.source: Starr, The Suzuki Violinist
Lin Yaoji, teaching maxim, in Yang Baozhi, Essentials of Lin Yaoji's Violin Teaching Method (2004)

phrases.text: playing too close to the fingerboard / too close to the bridge

rows.definition: Where on the string this player's bow usually sits during a recording, between the bridge and the fingerboard.
rows.unit: a share of the string's length
rows.range: 0 = at the bridge; bigger = closer to the fingerboard; one number for the whole recording
rows.prose: This records where the bow usually touches the string over a whole recording, between the bridge and the fingerboard. The number is zero at the bridge, and the bigger the number, the closer to the fingerboard. Teachers call this spot the "sounding point" or "contact point".
rows.short: the player's usual bow-contact spot
